import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Facility_Location")
    m.setParam("TimeLimit", 300)

    # Problem Data
    facilities = list(range(20))  # F0..F19
    customers = list(range(48))  # C0..C47

    # Facility coordinates (x, y)
    facility_coords = [(15, 46), (3, 85), (70, 21), (15, 77), (75, 10), (11, 71), (69, 4), (31, 17), (12, 43), (15, 60), (27, 59), (57, 22), (22, 41), (16, 7), (14, 17), (31, 42), (60, 33), (44, 14), (89, 76), (95, 43)]

    # Customer coordinates (x, y)
    customer_coords = [(79, 44), (9, 39), (66, 80), (14, 38), (61, 10), (87, 71), (65, 93), (51, 84), (98, 84), (61, 73), (94, 80), (30, 68), (35, 16), (43, 45), (78, 30), (94, 82), (92, 8), (64, 84), (19, 70), (84, 82), (81, 95), (61, 26), (20, 85), (93, 76), (92, 67), (58, 25), (87, 22), (21, 77), (92, 40), (27, 6), (67, 97), (29, 49), (12, 16), (40, 25), (9, 13), (31, 35), (5, 95), (38, 32), (18, 60), (83, 9), (73, 81), (9, 67), (37, 29), (12, 92), (91, 86), (10, 14), (9, 94), (65, 55)]

    facility_capacities = [181.0, 113.0, 129.0, 139.0, 187.0, 142.0, 186.0, 124.0, 96.0, 155.0, 147.0, 195.0, 200.0, 162.0, 165.0, 167.0, 108.0, 198.0, 134.0, 89.0]
    customer_demands = [40.0, 11.0, 41.0, 21.0, 24.0, 35.0, 12.0, 26.0, 44.0, 39.0, 18.0, 40.0, 47.0, 48.0, 19.0, 20.0, 48.0, 48.0, 43.0, 47.0, 43.0, 12.0, 35.0, 31.0, 37.0, 33.0, 39.0, 29.0, 45.0, 20.0, 27.0, 33.0, 29.0, 30.0, 50.0, 34.0, 41.0, 17.0, 29.0, 30.0, 42.0, 38.0, 14.0, 46.0, 31.0, 44.0, 26.0, 38.0]
    fixed_costs = [179.0, 484.0, 110.0, 172.0, 251.0, 219.0, 211.0, 219.0, 156.0, 379.0, 201.0, 291.0, 462.0, 202.0, 300.0, 397.0, 314.0, 200.0, 284.0, 484.0]
    transport_rate = 0.5  # $/km/unit

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates (INDUCED COSTS)
    def euclidean_distance(coord1, coord2):
        return math.sqrt((coord1[0] - coord2[0])**2 + (coord1[1] - coord2[1])**2)

    distances = {}
    for i in facilities:
        for j in customers:
            distances[(i, j)] = euclidean_distance(facility_coords[i], customer_coords[j])

    # Decision Variables
    # Open_F{i}: Binary - whether facility i is opened
    open_facility = {}
    for i in facilities:
        open_facility[i] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Open_F{i}")

    # Ship_F{i}_C{j}: Continuous - units shipped from facility i to customer j
    ship = {}
    for i in facilities:
        for j in customers:
            ship[(i, j)] = m.addVar(lb=0.0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_F{i}_C{j}")

    # Objective: Minimize fixed costs + transport costs
    # Transport cost = distance * rate * units shipped
    obj = quicksum(fixed_costs[i] * open_facility[i] for i in facilities)
    obj += quicksum(
        distances[(i, j)] * transport_rate * ship[(i, j)]
        for i in facilities for j in customers
    )
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Demand satisfaction constraints
    for j in customers:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(ship[(i, j)] for i in facilities) >= customer_demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_C{j}"
        )

    # Capacity constraints (can only ship if facility is open)
    for i in facilities:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(ship[(i, j)] for j in customers) <= facility_capacities[i] * open_facility[i],
            name=f"Capacity_F{i}"
        )

    m.optimize()
    return m

- A warehouse can only ship product if it is opened.
- Every customer’s demand must be fully covered.
- No warehouse can ship more than its capacity.

The goal is to minimize our total cost—combining the fixed spend to open warehouses with the variable spend to ship product—while ensuring every customer is served and no facility is over capacity. Once we confirm the preferred set of sites and assignments, we can lock in the opening plan and ramp up operations accordingly.
